title: Names with and without the 1
subtitle: France / the United States; Everest / the Alps
summary: Use no the with most names of people, countries, cities and mountains, but use the with oceans, rivers, deserts, plural names and names with Republic, Kingdom or States.

lesson.heading: Names without the
lesson.note: We do not use the with names of people, and in the same way we do not use the with most names of places.

lesson.heading: Republic, Kingdom, States
lesson.text: But we normally use the in names that contain a word like Republic, Kingdom or States.

examples.text: Have you been to **Canada** or **the United States**?

lesson.heading: Mr, Doctor, Captain, Mount, Lake
lesson.text: When we use Mr/Ms/Captain/Doctor/President etc. + a name, we do not use the. The same is true of Uncle, Saint and Queen, and of Mount (= mountain) and Lake before a name.

examples.text: We called **the doctor**. but We called **Doctor Johnson**.
**Mr Johnson** / **Captain Johnson** / **President Johnson** / **Uncle Robert** / **Saint Catherine** / **Queen Catherine**
They live near **the lake**. but They live near **Lake Superior**.

lesson.heading: Oceans, seas, rivers, canals, deserts: with the
lesson.text: We use the with the names of oceans, seas, rivers and canals, and also with the names of deserts.

examples.text: **the Atlantic** (Ocean), **the Indian Ocean**, **the Mediterranean** (Sea), **the Red Sea**

lesson.heading: Plural names: with the
lesson.text: We use the with plural names of people and places: families, countries with plural names, groups of islands and mountain ranges.

examples.text: The highest mountain in **the Andes** is (Mount) Aconcagua.

lesson.heading: the north of Brazil / northern Brazil

left.label: the north / the southeast (of ...)
examples: Sweden is in northern Europe; Spain is in **the south**.

lesson.note: We also use north/south etc. without the in the names of some regions and countries. On maps, the is not usually included in a name.

lesson.text: Single names (France, Everest, Lake Superior) take no the. Plural names and names with Republic / Kingdom / States (the Alps, the Netherlands, the UK) take the.

exercises.explanation: No the before a title + name: Doctor Johnson.

exercises.statement: In the United States, the President is elected for four years.
exercises.explanation: Correct. President here is used alone, not as a title + name, so the President. And the United States takes the.
Title + name takes no the: President Kennedy.

exercises.prompt: Julia spent three years as a student in ___.
exercises.explanation: Names with States, Kingdom or Republic take the.

exercises.statement: Milan and Turin are cities in north of Italy.
exercises.explanation: Milan and Turin are cities in the north of Italy. We say the north (of ...) but northern Italy.
Correct. Lake + name takes no the.

exercises.statement: Next year we're going skiing in Swiss Alps.
exercises.explanation: Next year we're going skiing in the Swiss Alps. Mountain ranges are plural names and take the.
Names of seas take the: the Caspian Sea.

exercises.prompt: Geography quiz: match each question with its answer.

pairs.left: What do you have to cross to travel from Europe to America?
Which is the longest river in Africa?
What is the name of the mountain range in the west of North America?
What is the name of the sea between Africa and Europe?
What joins the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans?

exercises.prompt: Of which country is Stockholm the capital? - ___
exercises.explanation: Most country names take no the: Sweden.

exercises.prompt: Does the name take the? Sort these names.
Put the words in order to say where the Seychelles are.
exercises.answer: The Seychelles are a group of islands in the Indian Ocean.
exercises.explanation: A group of islands (plural name) and an ocean both take the.
